task: Resolve the race condition in the session cache that causes stale session reads.

candidate_memories.content: Current test reproduces stale reads when two goroutines update the session cache within 50ms of each other.
Session cache writes must use a compare-and-swap operation to prevent lost updates under concurrent writes.
The session cache key format changed in the last sprint; the CAS operation must use the new key format.
Compare-and-swap is preferred over mutex locks for high-frequency cache updates to reduce contention.
The stale read issue does not affect read-only session queries; only writes need the CAS fix.
The session cache was migrated from Memcache to Redis in Q1.
User onboarding flow was redesigned with a new progress indicator in session 8.
Old cache note: session TTL was 2 hours before it was changed to 30 minutes.
Always invalidate related cache keys when updating a parent key.
The homepage A/B test was concluded with variant B winning in session 12.
Redis is also used for job queue state and feature flag caching.
Session 9 note: support team requested bulk user export capability.
Old session guide: session cache reads used a 100ms timeout before the SLA tightened.
Old lesson: Redis SETNX was the correct CAS operation before Lua scripting was available.
Memory profiling from session 11 showed no leaks in the session manager.
The mobile app connects to the session API through the API gateway.
The session expiry banner was added to the frontend in session 14.
The CDN is configured to bypass the cache for all /session/* routes.
Old practice: mutex locks were used for session cache updates before CAS was adopted.
Session data is replicated to a read replica for analytics queries.
